shorts.title: What you will learn: Structs
shorts.script: One variable, many fields. Today we make our own type. A struct groups related data, like the fields on an ID card. A struct groups related variables under one name. Each variable inside is a field. You define the struct once, and then you make as many variables of it as you like. The dot operator reaches one field. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Structs.

shorts.title: Structs in one minute
shorts.hook: A struct groups related variables under one name.
shorts.script: A struct groups related variables under one name. Each variable inside is a field. You define the struct once, and then you make as many variables of it as you like. The dot operator reaches one field. Think of an ID card. It is one card, but it holds a name, a class and a number. The struct has a name for the new type. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Structs in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: The function takes a const reference, as in episode twenty-five.
shorts.script: The function takes a const reference, as in episode twenty-five. No copy is made. Braces fill the fields in order. Asha gets the name, and ninety-one gets the marks. Ravi has seventy-eight. We call show for each student. The output has two lines. The program prints Asha colon ninety-one, and then Ravi colon seventy-eight. A struct groups related variables. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A missing semicolon after a struct
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. The struct has no semicolon after its closing brace. The compiler says expected semicolon after struct definition. A struct is a declaration, so it needs a semicolon. This is one of the most common beginner errors. A struct definition is a declaration, and every declaration ends with a semicolon. The compiler reads on and gets confused. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A missing semicolon after a struct.
